items.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Billy Taylor heard him when he came down here during the World’s Fair.

ctx.x: How early did he manifest this ability? It must have been . . . .

He could – it was like somebody as a kid who could fix anything, music or otherwise. He did manifest it at a young age. The 12 years that I spent at the New Orleans Center for Creative Arts, I don’t want to say that I was bitter, because I wasn’t, but I realized during those 12 years that the whole thing of talent is misconstrued by most people. I don’t necessarily mean coming up with a definition of it. I saw so many kids who came through and had serious talent. They either fell by the wayside with some drugs or…

We never did discourage our kids from playing, and like I said, I was always – always was able to find somebody who could teach the instrument and knew what they were doing. Unlike medicine, anybody can hang out a shingle and say “music teacher” and don’t go to jail.
